gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-sc: Wide, stretched and technical: Nulshock draws its outline in one unshaded line, spaced out generously. Noto Sans SC is the modest sans beside it, its chalky curves stopping well short of closing.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-syriac-: Technical to the core, Nulshock stretches wide with spacious tracking, while Noto Sans Syriac Western packs small letters tight with height. Nulshock earns its keep when it is big and short.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Noto Sans Tagalog lets its middle zone dominate the line, gaps in the curves staying generous, below bold Nulshock. One bends cable-like lines into shapes; the other lays down texture.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-oxygen: Nulshock stretches out wide, bold and technical, with no stroke modulation at all. Oxygen does the quieter work, its curves never closing back on themselves and its lowercase nearly matching the capitals.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-puritan: Stretched, bold, technical: Nulshock holds one constant stroke. Puritan, with rounded forms that stay open to the side and oversized counters, would keep paragraphs clean and approachable all the way down.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-schibsted-grotesk: A tube-like, constant-width stroke defines Nulshock, stretched and widely spaced. Schibsted Grotesk, with big open bowls and terminals that never close in, would carry paragraphs along in an approachable way.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-sen: Nulshock stretches wide, bold and technical, with spacious tracking and an unshaded outline. Sen counters that wide stance with lowercase built tall, a constant-weight line, and curves that end before turning inward.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-arimo: Sign-painter brushwork, single stroke, constant width: that is Origami. Arimo, a neutral sans with a tall mean line and spacious gaps in its round glyphs, gives the poured-lead lowercase room to breathe.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-mada: Origami draws a ruler-straight, single-stroke brush line with a lead-heavy lowercase. Mada, a sans-serif with a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close, would keep long paragraphs approachable and modern.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans: Poured-lead lowercase, brushed in one marker-steady stroke: that is Origami. Noto Sans steadies it with contemporary ease, its lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height and its c wide open.
